name: 5 CDSB Gagetown / Gagetown Range and Training Area
branch: Canadian Army / Department of National Defence
coordinate_source: NRCan Canadian Geographical Names Database (CGNDB) official feature DBDXI (Gagetown Range and Training Area, MIL). Official named-feature point; not a surveyed installation or range footprint.
coordinate_method: Official CGNDB military or populated-place feature uniquely named for this installation or training area.
known_energetics: Official pages describe an active range and training area used for Army individual and collective training, including schools of the Combat Training Centre. An IAAC project description for a proposed EOD range at 12 Wing Shearwater states that live ordnance and white phosphorus munitions from Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic are currently transported on public roads to 5 CDSB Gagetown for disposal. This draft does not have a current item-level inventory of munitions at Gagetown.
notable_incidents: 1966-06: National Defence’s Agent Orange investigations page states that for three days in June 1966, Agent Orange, Agent Purple, Agent White, and other herbicides were sprayed by the U.S. military at 5 CDSB Gagetown, with Canada’s permission, to test their effectiveness for vegetation management. The page says these 1966 and 1967 tests are the only known instances in which Agent Orange was tested on CAF property. [partly verified] | 1967-06: The same official page states that the U.S. military sprayed Agent Orange, Agent Purple, Agent White, and other herbicides at 5 CDSB Gagetown for four days in June 1967. It says the barrels were transported to the base by the U.S. military and records indicate they returned to the U.S. once testing was completed in 1967. It also states there is no evidence Agent Orange barrels were disposed of at the base, and that no barrels of Agent Orange have been found at Base Gagetown to date. [partly verified] | 2005: DND, with Veterans Affairs Canada, Health Canada and other departments, began a 2005–2007 fact-finding investigation of herbicide testing and use at Base Gagetown, including a historical review of herbicide use from 1952 to 2005, barrel investigations at 14 sites in 2005–2006, and human-health risk assessments. The official page says the Government of Canada later provided eligible individuals a one-time, tax-free ex gratia payment of $20,000 for possible exposure to unregistered U.S. herbicides between 1966 and 1967. [partly verified] | 2018-08: After a retired CAF member identified an area of interest near the former Shirley Road dump in June 2018, DND says an independent investigation in August 2018 of about 223 hectares identified 105 magnetic anomalies that were excavated. Items found included an ammo box and scrap metal; the official page states no barrels were found and that DND had no plans for further barrel-search activities at that time. [partly verified]
current_status: Active Canadian Army support base and range/training area. The official base page says 5 CDSB Gagetown opened in 1958 as a training facility and has an 1,100 square km training area. The main garrison is in Oromocto. As of the IAAC 90236 page checked on 2026-11-23, Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic still sends live ordnance and white phosphorus munitions to Gagetown for disposal. No open IAAC public-comment period for Gagetown was found on that date.
notes: Coordinates are the official NRCan CGNDB military feature 'Gagetown Range and Training Area' (geoname DBDXI), not a surveyed range footprint. A separately named official CGNDB feature 'Canadian Forces Base Gagetown' (DAABL) is at 45.833333, -66.45, nearer the Oromocto garrison described on the base page. Five former waste-disposal sites at the base are described on the Agent Orange investigations page (Shirley Road main dump, drum disposal area, asbestos dump area, chemical container disposal area, and ash disposal site); the chemical container disposal area was excavated and remediated in 1984. Those are contamination/disposal sites, not a current munitions inventory. A 2006 DND-wide herbicide review cited on that page concluded Agent Orange and other unregistered U.S. herbicides were only used at Base Gagetown among the CAF sites reviewed.

known_energetics: A 2015 DRDC article says large-scale blast and weapons trials are conducted on the Experimental Proving Ground (EPG), including historical 1960s trials that used 500 tonnes of TNT, and that weapons-system evaluations (the article names CRV-7 rockets, TOW missiles, various gun systems, and a test of the Excalibur artillery round) have been conducted there. notable_incidents: 1941: The 2015 DRDC article states that in 1941 the Canadian and British governments jointly procured 2,700 square kilometres of land to develop the Suffield Experimental Station (SES), described there as a chemical and biological weapons test facility used during the Second World War for countermeasures testing. [partly verified] | 1960s: The same official article says two of the largest explosives trials on the EPG, Operation Snowball and Operation Prairie Flat, were carried out in partnership with allied countries in the 1960s to provide technical information relatable to the detonation of nuclear weapons by creating an explosion using 500 tonnes of TNT. The article does not give a more precise year for either trial. [partly verified] | 1971: The DRDC article states that in 1971 the Canadian and British governments established CFB Suffield and designated a large portion of the Suffield Block as the Military Training Area for British Army Training Unit Suffield (BATUS). The remaining land, roughly 470 square kilometres, was permanently set aside for defence research and development as the Experimental Proving Ground. [partly verified]

name: Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot Dundurn
branch: Department of National Defence / Canadian Armed Forces
coordinate_source: NRCan Canadian Geographical Names Database (CGNDB) official feature HAASF (Camp Dundurn, UNP). Official named-feature point; not a surveyed installation or range footprint.
coordinate_method: Official CGNDB military or populated-place feature uniquely named for this installation or training area.
known_energetics: A May 2018 National Defence audit of ammunition and explosives management (footnote 11) lists Dundurn as one of four Canadian Forces ammunition depots, together with Angus, Bedford, and Rocky Point, and lists Bagotville, Cold Lake, and Wainwright as among the largest ammunition warehouses used in the audit’s FY 2015/16 data analysis. The audit describes ammunition and explosives examples as including small arms ammunition, missiles, torpedoes, explosive devices and pyrotechnics, as a class, not as a Dundurn-specific inventory. This draft does not have a current item-level inventory for CFAD Dundurn.
current_status: Officially identified in the May 2018 National Defence audit as one of four Canadian Forces ammunition depots. A current dedicated public depot webpage was not retrieved in this pass, so the record is based on that audit and on the official geographic name Camp Dundurn. This is a storage depot record; the retrieved official sources do not describe a current demolition or open-detonation range at Dundurn. No open IAAC public-comment period for Dundurn was found on 2026-11-23.
notes: Coordinates are the official NRCan CGNDB unincorporated place 'Camp Dundurn' (HAASF), a unique official populated-place name in Saskatchewan, not a surveyed depot footprint. A CGNDB query did not return a military feature named 'Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot Dundurn'. The town of Dundurn (TOWN HAGYA) is a separately named official feature nearby. An archived 2012–13 National Defence installations list also named Canadian Forces Ammunition Depot Dundurn in Dundurn, SK; that list is archived and is used only as supporting historical context, not as proof of present-day operations on its own. The other three depots named in the 2018 audit (Angus, Bedford, Rocky Point) are not added as separate records in this pass.

name: 12 Wing Shearwater — proposed Explosive Ordnance Disposal Range
branch: Department of National Defence / Royal Canadian Navy (Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic) / Royal Canadian Air Force (12 Wing)
coordinate_source: NRCan Canadian Geographical Names Database (CGNDB) official feature CCAAV (12 Wing Shearwater, MIL). Official named-feature point; not a surveyed installation or range footprint.
coordinate_method: Official CGNDB military or populated-place feature uniquely named for this installation or training area.
known_energetics: The IAAC 90236 project description says the proposed EOD range would include a fenced sand-pit area with a berm for disposal of white phosphorus munitions, a fenced area with dirt or fine gravel and a berm for disposal of other conventional unexploded ordnance, and an operational readiness suite (demolition bunker) made from an intermodal shipping container with protective works. It also states that live ordnance and white phosphorus munitions are currently transported on public roads to 5 CDSB Gagetown for disposal.
notable_incidents: 2026-03-10: The public comment period on IAAC registry 90236 (proposed EOD range at 12 Wing Shearwater) closed on 10 March 2026. The official project description states that Joint Task Force Atlantic does not have an EOD range in the Halifax area for munitions tasked for disposal by the Royal Canadian Navy’s Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic, and that live ordnance and white phosphorus munitions are currently transported on public roads to 5 CDSB Gagetown in Oromocto, New Brunswick, for safe disposal. As of 2026-11-23 the assessment remained in progress with no posted determination. [partly verified]
current_status: Proposed DND project on federal lands; not confirmed as constructed. IAAC registry 90236 public comments closed on 10 March 2026. As of the registry page checked on 2026-11-23, the assessment status was still 'In progress', and DND was considering comments before determining whether the project is likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects. No determination had been posted, and the comment period was not open.
notes: Coordinates are the official NRCan CGNDB military feature '12 Wing Shearwater' (CCAAV), used only as an approximate location for the wing. They are not a surveyed footprint of the proposed EOD range, whose exact layout is not published as coordinates on the IAAC page retrieved for this pass. This record is a proposed facility, not an operating range confirmed by a determination or a DND 'now open' notice.
